Published under Transactions on Substrate Engineering (Alexanarch deposit #1742) via the Provenance Erasure project, the notebook examines how scientific findings and public summaries handled data surrounding the interstellar comet [3I/ATLAS](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESYwHEIkXXg1BkVMG89_YNO-4TptP__pOM-92sJ8tYBaWZgLdEjVPU3uEO6xaTkDmN67Z0KGw-Yes6WWrsBdoyNZZspeE3GX5ocn--Phv6SEtF4QRu_0X8Q7cLokZvlvzknENI9w). [1] Key Themes of the Notebook * Framing of Avi Loeb's Stance. The notebook critiques how automated summaries portrayed astrophysicist Avi Loeb's July 2025 comment ("most likely natural") as a later December retreat toward mainstream consensus, noting he consistently held the object at Level 4 on his anomaly scale. * Radio Search Limitations. It analyzes the scope of the Allen Telescope Array (ATA) radio search, pointing out that its drift-rate filter only retained positive drift rates even though the object's ephemeris predicted a negative drift rate, while public summaries framed the null result as ruling out all active transmitters. * Breakthrough Listen Data Review. Examining public Green Bank Telescope data from December 18, 2025, the authors note thirteen weak, unreplicated spectral features between 1665.53 and 1668.46 MHz (near the comet's hydroxyl lines) that fell below standard detection thresholds, though they explicitly stop short of calling them transmissions. * Provenance Erasure & Sophistry Measure. The document uses 3I/ATLAS as a case study to test a framework measuring how scientific context, caveats, and attribution get altered or stripped away as information moves from raw data to press releases and AI summaries.
